title: OpenAI is building ‘a family of devices,’ Greg Brockman confirms
excerpt: The president says voice will replace typing and the hardware is coming ‘soon,’ while brushing off Apple’s lawsuit: “we have no interest in other companies’ trade secrets.” OpenAI is not building one gadget but several, its pres
content_html:
The president says voice will replace typing and the hardware is coming ‘soon,’ while brushing off Apple’s lawsuit: “we have no interest in other companies’ trade secrets.”

OpenAI is not building one gadget but several, its president Greg Brockman has confirmed, describing “a family of devices” in an interview that put the company’s long-rumoured hardware ambitions on the record.

Speaking to the journalist Joanna Stern, Brockman said the products are coming “soon,” without offering a date.The confirmation ends little suspense but adds some shape.

OpenAI has spent a year assembling a hardware effort around Jony Ive, the former Apple design chief whose screen-free speaker has already leaked, and Brockman’s “family” language suggests the speaker is only the first of a range.

OpenAI bought its way into the effort. It acquired Ive’s hardware startup, io, in a multibillion-dollar deal, folding a team of former Apple engineers into a company that had never shipped a physical product, which is part of what Apple’s lawsuit is now about. The deal made OpenAI a hardware company overnight, at least on paper.

Brockman’s pitch rests on a single bet: that talking beats typing. Voice, he said, is “a far more natural way to interact with a machine,” the premise behind a device meant to be spoken to rather than tapped, and the reason OpenAI thinks it can build hardware around ChatGPT rather than an app.

He was vaguer on everything else. Asked to confirm the rumoured smart speaker, Brockman neither denied nor detailed it, folding the question back into his “family of devices” line, a practised non-answer from a company that has learned to tease without committing.

The interview’s sharper moment was about Apple. The iPhone maker is suing OpenAI, alleging former staff carried hardware trade secrets across to the AI firm, a case that has thrown a shadow over the whole device project.

“We have no interest in other companies’ trade secrets. We are plenty innovative,” he said, declining to go further on the active litigation but making clear OpenAI intends to fight rather than settle quietly.

The dispute is not costless. Apple’s suit has already complicated OpenAI’s hardware plans, a reminder that building physical products drags a software firm into unfamiliar and expensive legal terrain.

The ambition behind the devices is large. OpenAI is not only making a speaker; it is reportedly working on a phone with Qualcomm and MediaTek, aiming at hundreds of millions of shipments a year by the end of the decade, an assault on the market Apple built.

That framing explains Apple’s alarm. A “family of devices” built around voice and ChatGPT is, in the long run, a bid to replace the phone as the thing people reach for, which is precisely the market Apple cannot afford to cede.

The competition is already crowded. Meta is betting on smart glasses, Amazon has spent a decade trying to make Alexa a platform, and Google keeps folding its assistant into everything, so OpenAI is entering a race rather than opening one.

Whether OpenAI can pull it off is another matter. Hardware is unforgiving, margins are thin, and the graveyard of ambitious AI gadgets, from pins to pendants, is already crowded with products that promised to end the smartphone and instead ended themselves.

Brockman’s confidence rests on distribution. OpenAI has hundreds of millions of ChatGPT users and a partner in Ive who knows how to make objects people want, a combination few rivals can match, whatever the courts eventually decide about how the designs were made.

For now, the news is the shape of the plan. Not one device but many, built for the voice, arriving “soon,” and defended in advance against an Apple lawsuit that OpenAI is treating as a nuisance rather than a threat.

The next move belongs to the calendar. OpenAI has confirmed the what and the why; the when, and whether the first of these devices lands before the legal fight is resolved, is the part Brockman was careful not to pin down.

content_html_zh:
总统表示语音将取代打字，硬件“很快”就会推出，同时对苹果的诉讼不予理睬：“我们对其他公司的商业秘密没有兴趣。”

OpenAI 总裁格雷格·布罗克曼 (Greg Brockman) 证实，OpenAI 并不是在制造一个设备，而是在制造多个设备，他在一次采访中描述了“一系列设备”，这也公开了该公司传闻已久的硬件野心。

布罗克曼在接受记者乔安娜·斯特恩采访时表示，这些产品“很快”就会上市，但没有透露具体日期。这一确认结束了一些悬念，但增加了一些形状。

OpenAI 花了一年的时间围绕前苹果设计主管 Jony Ive 组装硬件，他的无屏扬声器已经泄露，而布罗克曼的“家族”语言表明该扬声器只是该系列中的第一个。

OpenAI 也参与其中。 它以数十亿美元的价格收购了 Ive 的硬件初创公司 io，将一支前苹果工程师团队并入一家从未发货过实体产品的公司，这也是苹果现在诉讼的一部分。 这笔交易让 OpenAI 一夜之间成为一家硬件公司，至少在纸面上是这样。

布罗克曼的主张基于一个赌注：说话胜过打字。 他说，语音是“一种更自然的与机器交互的方式”，这是设备背后的前提，旨在与人交谈而不是点击，这也是 OpenAI 认为它可以围绕 ChatGPT 而不是应用程序构建硬件的原因。

他对其他事情都比较模糊。 当被要求证实传闻中的智能音箱时，布罗克曼既没有否认，也没有详细说明，而是将这个问题重新纳入了他的“设备家族”系列中，这是一家学会了戏弄而不承诺的公司惯常的不回答。

这次采访最尖锐的时刻是关于苹果的。 这家 iPhone 制造商正在起诉 OpenAI，指控其前员工向这家 AI 公司携带硬件商业机密，这一案件给整个设备项目蒙上了阴影。

“我们对其他公司的商业秘密没有兴趣。 我们有很多创新精神。”他拒绝进一步讨论正在进行的诉讼，但明确表示 OpenAI 打算进行斗争，而不是安静地和解。

这场纠纷并非没有代价。 苹果的诉讼已经使 OpenAI 的硬件计划变得复杂，这提醒人们，构建实体产品会将软件公司拖入不熟悉且昂贵的法律领域。

这些设备背后的野心是巨大的。 OpenAI 不仅仅制造扬声器；据报道，该公司正在与高通和联发科合作开发一款手机，目标是到本世纪末，每年出货量达到数亿部，这是对苹果建立的市场的一次进攻。

这个框架解释了苹果的警报。 从长远来看，围绕语音和 ChatGPT 构建的“设备家族”将取代手机成为人们所追求的东西，而这正是苹果无法放弃的市场。

比赛已经人满为患。 Meta 将赌注押在智能眼镜上，亚马逊花了十年时间试图将 Alexa 打造成一个平台，谷歌不断将其助手融入到一切事物中，因此 OpenAI 正在进入一场竞赛，而不是开启一场竞赛。

OpenAI 能否成功则是另一回事。 硬件是无情的，利润微薄，从别针到吊坠等雄心勃勃的人工智能小玩意的墓地已经挤满了那些承诺终结智能手机但实际上却终结了自己的产品。

布罗克曼的信心在于分销。 OpenAI 拥有数亿 ChatGPT 用户和 Ive 合作伙伴，他知道如何制造人们想要的物体，这是很少有竞争对手可以匹敌的组合，无论法院最终决定如何设计。

目前，新闻只是该计划的雏形。 不是一种设备，而是许多种专为语音而设计的设备，“即将”到来，并提前针对苹果公司的诉讼进行了辩护，OpenAI 将其视为一种滋扰而不是威胁。

下一步行动属于日历。 OpenAI 已经确认了内容和原因；布罗克曼小心翼翼地没有透露这些设备何时落地，以及是否会在法律纠纷解决之前落地。
